html:
A Vietnamese religious movement founded in 1939 by Huỳnh Phú Sổ in the village of Hòa Hảo in the Mekong delta. It is a reformed lay Buddhism with between one and several million followers, most of them farmers in the delta.

Huỳnh Phú Sổ, a young man known as a healer and prophet, taught that faith should be simple and practised at home, without costly temples, statues or clergy. Followers pray before a plain altar and give help to the poor. The movement spread fast among the peasants of the western delta, under French rule and then Japanese occupation.

It soon had its own armed forces. In the wars of the 1940s it fought the French, the communist Viet Minh and other groups, and the Viet Minh killed Huỳnh Phú Sổ in 1947. In 1955 and 1956 Ngô Đình Diệm, president of South Vietnam, crushed its army. After 1975 the communist government restricted it, and a state approved branch was recognised in 1999. Like the Cao Đài faith, it shows the religious ferment of colonial Vietnam.
